terminal.description: A shell in your workspace where try.js asks your API for pages, filters and sort orders of the fleet.

tasks.title: Read the query string
tasks.description:
Implement `parseListQuery(searchParams)` in `src/listQuery.js`. It takes a `URLSearchParams` and returns `{ type, available, sortBy, order, limit, offset }`:

| Parameter | Accepts | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | one of `BOAT_TYPES` | `null` |
| `available` | `true` or `false`, returned as a boolean | `null` |
| `sort` | `code`, `name` or `hourlyCents`, with a leading `-` for descending; sets `sortBy` and `order` (`'asc'` or `'desc'`) | `sortBy: 'code'`, `order: 'asc'` |
| `limit` | a whole number from 1 to 50 | `10` |
| `offset` | a whole number from 0 | `0` |

Unknown parameters are ignored. A whole number is written with digits only, so `2.5`, `10abc`, `1e3` and an empty value are all bad. When any value is bad, throw `new HttpError(400, 'invalid_query', message, details)` with one `{ field, message }` per bad parameter, every problem at once.
nextSteps: Start from an object holding the defaults.
Read each parameter with `searchParams.get` and handle `null` as not given.
Write one small helper for whole numbers and use it for limit and offset.
Collect problems and throw once at the end, then press Check.
hints: Everything in a query string is text. Your job is to turn text into typed values, or say clearly why you cannot.
`Number('')` is 0 and `parseInt('10abc')` is 10, so neither is strict enough on its own. A regular expression that only matches digits is.
For sort, check `sort.startsWith('-')`, slice it off, then check what is left against the three field names.

tasks.title: Filter, sort and page
tasks.description:
Implement `applyListQuery(boats, query)` in `src/listQuery.js`. It takes the boats and a query shaped like the result of `parseListQuery`, and returns `{ data, total, limit, offset }`:

- keep the boats whose `type` and `available` match; a `null` value means no filter
- sort by `sortBy` in `order`; boats with the same value are ordered by `code`, ascending, in both directions
- `total` is the number of matching boats **before** paging
- `data` holds at most `limit` boats, starting at `offset`; an offset past the end gives `[]`

It must not change the order of the `boats` array it is given. The check runs it on the fleet in reverse order.
nextSteps: Filter first, keeping the result in a new array.
Write a compare function for the sort that falls back to the code.
Run `node try.js` once the route is done too.
hints: Filter, sort, count, slice. The order of these steps decides what total means.
`available: false` is a filter. A check like `if (query.available)` skips it by accident.
`filter` returns a new array, so sorting that one is safe. In the compare function, multiply the field comparison by -1 for desc, and use `|| compareCodes` for ties.

tasks.title: Serve the list
tasks.description:
Fill in `listBoats` in `src/app.js` so `GET /boats` answers `200` with the envelope `{ data, total, limit, offset }`.

- read the query string from `req.url`
- parse it with `parseListQuery`
- apply it to `store.list()` with `applyListQuery`

A bad parameter answers `400` with code `invalid_query` and its details. The check also creates a boat and then lists it, so the list must come from the store.
nextSteps: Run `node try.js` and read every answer.
hints: You already took the pathname out of `req.url` in handleRequest. The same object has the query.
`new URL(req.url, 'http://localhost').searchParams` is exactly what parseListQuery takes.
Do not catch the HttpError from parseListQuery. createApp already turns it into a 400.
